purpose_of_this_fixture: The document fixture (A16, WP18): not a transcript fixture. Three client documents and one short call. The documents: a client SOP as a Word file (QP-07, version 3.2, with an author, a date and a status on its front page and in its core metadata), a flowchart as a PNG image (Figure 1, QP-07-F1, twelve nodes with two decision diamonds and labelled exits, no metadata), and a requirements write-up as a PDF with no author, date or status anywhere. The call: fifteen minutes with the Sample Reception Coordinator, the operator who runs the documented process, in which she says the documented priority-approval step (QP-07 section 4.2) is not used. Fictional client: an independent seed-testing laboratory. It proves that each document is measured, saved unchanged into inputs/ and stopped at the same open question as a transcript [A11-3]; that author, date and status are recorded from the SOP and left unknown on the figure and the write-up, with no author invented; that the SOP's sections feed current state while the write-up feeds the requirement trace and never the current-state picture; that the flowchart's steps and decision points become documented rows in the structure inventory citing the page; that every extract is [Q/doc] by document and section or page and never by speaker, at the attributed tier for the SOP and one step below for the write-up and the figure; that the document-versus-call disagreement on the priority approval is kept as a conflict with both sources and offered as a callback, never resolved by recency and never discarded; and that the record grades twice: document-only first, with no type header, nothing advisory, the current-state and requirements criteria Met from the documents (each with a residual) and cost, why-now, decision and next step Missing with every gap shown, then with the call, where the operator's figure grades as a client figure and the verdict becomes Nearly ready. Taking the call first and the documents after ends in the same record (intake.grading_passes.arrival_orders).

entities_and_workflows: Sample receipt (QP-07 section 3): a consignment arrives by courier, post or hand; the Sample Reception Coordinator checks it against the test request (QF-03), gives it the next sample number, enters it in the register (lived: the day book first, then the spreadsheet), stamps the form into the tray and labels the container into the receipt store (a locked cupboard with a sealed section for moisture samples).

Allocation (section 4.1): each morning the Laboratory Supervisor allocates the previous day's samples to the benches in order of receipt on the bench allocation sheet; lived: the Laboratory Manager prints the previous day's register and writes the bench on it in biro.

Priority requests (section 4.2): documented as approved by the Laboratory Manager before allocation, initials and date on the form and in the register, then allocated at the head of the next allocation; lived: nobody uses the box, reception puts the sample at the top of the pile and tells whoever is on purity, the Laboratory Manager finds out from the list if she looks. Kept as the conflict.

Re-tests (section 4.3): a re-test starts only on a re-test request (QF-12) authorised by the Laboratory Manager, its number recorded on the bench sheet; lived: used, the bench will not start without the form, checked against the forms monthly.

Testing (section 5): the analyst tests by the methods manual, records on the bench sheet, enters results into the results database on completion and signs the sheet; if the database is down, results wait on the sheet.
Review (sections 6.1 and 6.2): a second analyst checks the database against the bench sheet and initials it; a result outside tolerance goes to a re-test under section 4.3.

Certification (sections 6.3 and 6.4): reception prepares the certificate from the template by transcribing results from the database and checking them; the Laboratory Manager or the Quality Manager signs; the issue date goes in the register. Lived: every number checked twice, ten to fifteen minutes each, thirty a day in the season; a transposed result reissued in June.

Turnaround (section 6.5): 21 days for germination and vigour, 10 for purity and moisture, 7 for an approved priority; lived: not measured in progress, the Quality Manager counts monthly from the register's dates, lateness is learned from the submitter's call.
Enquiries (section 3.4): reception establishes a sample's status with the bench and answers the same day; lived: walking the benches or ringing and waiting, about two hours a day.
Records (section 7): bench sheets, requests and certificate copies kept six years; the register backed up weekly.

leanings.question: Is a sample one row with one bench and one status, or a parent with one child row per test?
leanings.option: A child row per test requested, each with its bench, its status and its due date under section 6.5 (7 days once a priority is approved); the sample's status and its latest due date roll up; the priority flag sits on the sample and shows on every child. One row with one bench column is the register's own flaw: a multi-test sample is on two benches at once, and in September purity finished the day it arrived while germination queued for a week.
quotes: Fifteen if it's a multi-test.
And purity was fine, purity did it that day. But germination's a seven-day test and nobody on germination knew it was urgent, so it went in the normal queue, and it came out the Thursday after.
Certificates are normally issued within 21 days of receipt for germination and vigour tests and within 10 days of receipt for purity and moisture tests.
leanings.condition: The Laboratory Manager confirms on the 9th that a multi-test sample is worked by more than one bench at the same time and says how many samples a day carry more than one test; if nearly every sample is single-test, one row with a bench per test column is the fallback.
leanings.pattern: one row where the call describes many

leanings.question: Who sets a test's status at the bench, when the analysts will not touch a screen?
leanings.option: The Laboratory Manager's morning allocation sets each test's bench and 'allocated' on the board; 'started' and 'results entered' are set by the one analyst who will touch a screen or on a shared screen at the bench; reception never keys a bench status she learned by walking, because that would be today's walk with a board in front of it. Any status a person sets is that person's claim; the bench sheet and the results database stay the evidence.
quotes: The analysts have got seed dust on their hands all day, they're not going to touch a screen. Tobiah will, the others won't.
Analysts must not need a keyboard at the bench while they are handling seed.
leanings.condition: The Laboratory Manager's answer on the 9th: a scan, a shared screen at the bench, the morning sheet, or herself alone; until then no bench view is shown as live.

leanings.question: Does an approval step sit behind the priority flag, and whose is it?
leanings.option: The priority flag on the sample with a notification to the Laboratory Manager is built; the approval step is built neither way. If the 9th settles on the procedure, the approval becomes a status the Laboratory Manager sets on the sample (W-3) and the 7-day target starts from it; if it settles on reception's route, the flag alone, with the notification as the Laboratory Manager's sight of it.

leanings.question: Can the certificate be prepared from recorded results in the first version?
leanings.option: Not yet. The certificate stage is a status with prepared, signed and sent dates; no result is held on the platform; the draft from recorded results waits for a read from the results database (an export, a report or read access) that nobody has described or granted. Until then the template is typed as today, and the structure copies today's tool for the three P2 pains.

leanings.question: What happens to a prepared certificate draft when a result changes after it?
leanings.option: The draft carries the date of the results it was prepared from; a later results-entered or re-test date on any of the sample's tests resets 'prepared' and shows a reissue. By the procedure a re-test precedes any certificate, but the June reissue shows a certificate can be wrong after it is signed.
